p.t: In short
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Pick **one or two** research tools. Cancel any tool that finds no useful products in about one month.
Every paid tool is a **monthly cost** you must cover before sales arrive. Budget for it before you have revenue.
Free ad libraries (public lists of ads) come first. A paid spy tool is worth it only when you have a **specific product or niche** in mind.
Your own ads decide whether a product works. Tools only help you choose what to test.
Spy tools show what competitor stores sell and run. Check which plan includes the features you need before paying.
SimilarWeb estimates how many visitors a store gets. Check the **country rank** for the country you plan to sell in.
Bundles claim big savings. Count only the tools you really use, and **cancel** any tool with no job.
Never keep winning products in a shared account. **Export** your research and save it yourself.
Kalodata is a research tool that shows which TikTok Shop products, videos and creators sell best.

Set the country to **United States** before you read any ranking, because results change by country.
Use AI (ChatGPT) only for a rough first look at a niche.
Check any AI result against real sales numbers before you trust it.
Choosing tools and limiting spend
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Pay for a research tool (a program that finds product ideas) for **about one month**, then cancel

if it does not find useful products in that time.
Use a strict rule: invest in **one or two tools** to find around 10 to 50 products in a month.
Start with only **one or two** research tools that you will use every week.
Each subscription (a payment you make every month) is a fixed cost. You must cover it before any sales arrive.
An ad spy tool (a program that shows other sellers' ads) is worth its cost only when you have a **specific product or niche** in mind. A niche is a small, focused market.
Example: checking which shoes, slippers or bags perform best in one market before you sell in another.

For general product research with no clear goal, an ad spy tool is **not worth the expense**.
Research and spy tools often cost **$15 to $99 per month** each.
Some cost more. Pipiads and PPSpy cost about $263 and $299 per month on the list prices shown.
A new store should budget these as **fixed monthly costs** before it has revenue to cover them.

Pick **one spy tool** and use it consistently for product searches and keyword checks.
The source names Dropispy, Peeksta, Adspy and Minea as options.
Saturation-checking tools (tools that show how crowded a market is, meaning how many sellers already sell the same product) can help screen competition.
They do **not replace a small paid test**. The Facebook data from your own ads decides whether a product works.
Some sellers hide their store from spy tools by **paying the tool operators** to remove them.
Other sellers add code to the store that blocks scraping (automatically copying data from a web page).
The mentor reported these methods but has not tested them.
Niche validation and market data
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: The Source A Research Tool gives **real data** from trusted sources for niche research.
It saves hundreds of hours of manual research.
Open it on the online platform.
For any niche you enter, it shows grade, average price, demographic appeal (how well a product appeals to different groups of people), brand loyalty, seasonality (how demand rises

and falls through the year) and demand.
Use it for **all market data** in your niche selection process.
The Source A research software has **unlimited use**.
It shows a niche's monthly Google search volume (how many times people search for it each month), its seasonality verdict and its average price analysis **within seconds**.
It can test any number of niches, not only a short list.
Set up your research workspace (your working screen) with the worksheet on the left half and the research tool on the right half in **split-screen view** (two windows side by side).
You can also open the tool in its own browser tab.
Copy each niche keyword (the search word for the niche) from the worksheet and paste it into the tool **without switching back and forth**.
Source A Research Software is a Source A research tool named in an **October 2025** coaching call (a live training session with a mentor).

The document only lists it. It does not describe its features.
Research tools for members are at the source's own site
They use the same login as the Blueprint program.
Niche Verification is a tool for checking **whether a niche is worth pursuing** before you commit money and time to it.
Google Trends is the primary tool for checking demand and seasonality for a product.
Set the region and a **five-year time range** to see whether demand is steady, spiky (sudden peaks) or truly seasonal.
The Fast Business Forum (fastbusinessforum.com) is used to search for niche selection advice from other sellers.

You need to be **logged in to post**.
Send private messages by clicking a member's name.
Free ad libraries
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: An ad library is a public list of ads that anyone can search.
The Meta Ad Library is a **free** tool that shows active ads (ads running right now) from advertisers.
p.h: Meta ad library and Facebook ad library

p.t:
It shows how many ads a creative runs in. A creative is the picture or video of an ad.
Use it to study competitors (other sellers in your niche).
Look for creatives that run in **many ads**. Check which hooks (the first lines or seconds that grab attention) big brands keep using.

The Meta Ad Library shows **every** active ad a brand runs.
For each ad it shows the start date, format and copy (the written words of the ad).
It is reached from a competitor's page under **Page transparency** (a Facebook section that shows a page's details).

The country can be changed to show regional ads.
The Meta Ad Library is a free tool that shows all running ads.
**Filter by country**, search by keyword or brand, and screenshot ads for inspiration.
The Meta Ad Library is a free, public Meta database (a large store of data run by Meta, the company behind Facebook).

You can search currently running ads by keyword and see which pages and stores run them.
Use it to find competitor stores through the ads they run.

The Facebook Ad Library lets you search by **country, category and keyword or advertiser name**.
It shows the ads a competitor is running on Facebook.
Check competitor ads for the same niche title in the **TikTok Ads Library**, the Facebook Ads Library and the Meta Ad Library.
Bookmark them (save the page link) next to Kalodata (a TikTok sales research tool, see below) for quick access.
Use the Ads Library **filters** to show active ads and sort by active ads. You can also see summary details.

Use the link from each ad to check the store and its other ads.
AdLib (a tool that works with the Facebook Ad Library) connects to the Facebook Ad Library.

Click **download** in AdLib to save videos and thumbnails (small preview pictures) directly.
Or use the Facebook Ad Library link for manual downloads.
Winning Hunter (a paid research tool, see below) offers a **free Chrome extension** (a small add-on for the Chrome web browser).
It works with the Meta Ad Library. Install it when you want to pull ads into Winning Hunter's analysis views.
Ad spy tools in general
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Ad spy tools track competitor ads and creatives. They show which ads are running for big brands.
Use them to find the creatives a niche is **scaling** (putting more money into ads that already sell) before you test similar hooks.
Ad spy tools such as Pinterest, Snapchat and TikTok searches can show **winning products** (products that sell well).
The seller runs Facebook and TikTok side by side to see which platform works better for a product.

Minea and Dropispy show ads and competitor products across platforms.
They are used for **product research** (finding products to sell).
Spy tools show what competitors advertise and which products they sell.
Tools such as Foreplay, Adspy and Dropispy are used for this kind of ad and product research.
AfterLive adds extra filters on top of Meta Ad Library data.
p.h: Paid Meta and Facebook ad spy tools: AfterLive

p.t: The filters include active ads count, country, platform and a **30-day performance view** (how an ad did over the last 30 days).

The mentor considered it the **best tool** for finding recent ads on Meta.
It starts at about **$50 to $80 per month**, with a free trial.

Other spy tools mostly show older ads.
Some sellers can block those tools.
The source names this tool **Afterlip**, with a **$9 per month** plan, down from $99 per month.
Its features may differ from the full plan shown in the example. Compare the plan's feature list with the example before you assume the same functions are available.

AfterLive setup:
Set **Technology** to Shopify.
Set countries to United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

Set the call-to-action (the button text on the ad) to **Shop Now or Learn More**.
Set the **Active Ads minimum** to 10.

Set the Performance filter to the **last 30 days**.
The Performance view shows a progression (a timeline) of new active ads per day over the chosen period.

It lets you see a competitor's launch pattern.
The Trending view highlights competitors scaling aggressively in a shorter time.
A **7-day** data option is available for very recent winners.
DropiSpy
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
DropiSpy research setup:
Set the date filter to **the last one month**.

Set minimum thresholds (limits) for likes, shares and comments.
Set the e-com platform (online store software) to **Shopify**.
Set the call-to-action to Shop Now or Learn More.

Set countries to United States, Canada, Australia and United Kingdom.
DropiSpy costs about **$29 per month** at list price (the normal published price).

With a discount code, it costs about $15 to $20 per month.
Rental platforms that resell tool logins sometimes list it for about $2 to $10 per month.
A bundle price screenshot (several tools sold together) lists Dropispy at **$249 per month**.

The two figures conflict. The $29 list price applies to the provider's own plan. The $249 is the bundle's list price.
Check the **current price** on the provider's site before buying.

AdSpy is a paid Facebook ad spy tool costing **$150 per month**.
It lets you search by keyword.

It lets you filter by a date range, such as ads started since January 1.
It lets you sort ads by likes or shares to spot trends.
AdSpy is an ad library for searching competitor ads by keyword, age, gender, country and store URL (the store's web address).

A free account gives up to **20 pages** of search per day.
If AdSpy asks you to buy an account, **do not pay** for it.
Create a new account and use the free search.

If your email was used on an earlier account, sign up with a **new email address**.
AdSpy finds older Facebook ads, such as those from 2019 and 2020.
It was considered **expensive**. Compare its monthly cost with alternatives such as Peeksta.
Peeksta (peeksta.com) and adtargeting.io help find **niche-specific Meta interests** (topics Facebook uses to target people).
They help build single-interest test ad sets (ad groups aimed at one interest only).
Peeksta is an ad spy tool used to find older Facebook ads, such as those from 2019 and 2020.

It was presented as a cheaper alternative to Adspy, at about **$50 per month**.
The price figures in the source do not agree. Check the current price before you subscribe.

Peeksta is used for **product research**, to find products that are performing well.
It is a paid-style research tool referenced for locating winning products.
AfterLib
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: AfterLib is a paid product research tool, costing about **$150 per month**.

It ranks products by performance or by number of active ads.
It is used to build the first candidate list (a short list of possible products).
Check each product manually in the Facebook Ad Library after that.
AfterLib is a paid ad spy tool recommended for its large library and its data on how competitors scale their ads.

It shows an ad's progression. This means the growing number of ads per creative over time.
A rising progression signals a profitable product.
AfterLib shows how the ad activity of a product changes over time.
Use it to spot products whose ads have risen by roughly **100 to 300 percent** in the last 14 days.

AfterLib is considered expensive compared with Peeksta.
It offers a free trial of about **7 to 14 days**.

Its data is pulled from the Ad Library itself.
Experienced sellers consider its sales tracker accurate.
AfterLib sign-up accepts a public discount code (a code anyone can use), **SAVE10**, for 10 percent off.
Sellers who want 25 to 30 percent can ask the vendor's support team directly for a larger discount.
AfterLib shared-access membership: a team plan (one account for several people) allows several people to log in to one AfterLib account.

The reported price for one person's shared access is **$6.99**.
AfterLib filter setup:
1. Click **All filters**.
2. Under Technology, choose **Shopify**.
3. Under Country, select the target country. For a general setup, use United States, United Kingdom, Canada, New Zealand and Australia.
AfterLib (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
4. Under Language, choose **English**.
5. Under Call to action, choose **Shop now and Learn more**.
6. Under Creation date (when the ad was first made), prefer the **last 30 to 45 days** to find recently launched ads. Results are already sorted by performance, so this step is less critical.

AfterLib steps to reach the competitor's Facebook Ad Library page:
1. Click the **three dots** next to the product result.

2. Click **Go to meta page** to open the competitor's Facebook Ad Library page.
3. Apply the **Active ads** filter.
4. Count the active ads for the product only.
5. Subtract any active ads that belong to other products the competitor is testing on the same page. Then record the adjusted number.
Mynia is an alternative ad spy tool with data for Facebook, Pinterest and TikTok.
It shows likes, comments, shares, page creation date, the audience targeted and other competitors fetched for the same search.

Mynia combines Pinterest, Facebook and TikTok ads in **one place**.
It is used to spot new products. It also shows which competitors run ads across platforms.

Mynia filter setup for Facebook product research:
1. Log in and open the ad section. Then select **Facebook**.

2. Under date, choose the creation date filter for the **last 30 days**.
3. Under CTA, choose Buy now, Shop now and Learn more.

4. Under ecommerce platform, choose **Shopify**.
5. Under language, choose **English**.
6. Set engagement minimums (likes, comments and shares): at least **200 likes**, at least 100 comments and at least 100 shares.

7. Select countries: United States, United Kingdom, Australia and Canada.
Mynia has no direct link to the competitor's Ad Library. Use this path:

1. Open the ad post in Mynia.
2. Click the **page name**.
3. Open the About section and then **Page transparency**.

4. Click **See all** and scroll down to Go to ad library.
5. On the Ad Library page, click **active ads** and count the ads for the specific product.
Winning Hunter
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Winning Hunter is a paid research tool that uses AI (artificial intelligence, software that finds patterns and writes text).

Winning Hunter is the **AI product research tool** recommended for finding candidate products.
It is preferred over Kalodata, which was used earlier.
Winning Hunter is preferred for product research.
Kalodata remains useful as one signal source (a place that shows a sign of demand). Use it alongside TikTok Shop and competitor stores.
The Brands tracker shows **one overview** of a Meta advertiser (a business that runs Facebook or Instagram ads).

The overview covers top ad copies, headlines, hooks, landing pages (the page a visitor reaches after clicking an ad), personas (made-up buyer profiles), concepts, angles (the way an ad frames the problem),
desires, emotions, awareness stages (how aware a buyer is of the problem) and USPs (unique selling points, the main reason to buy).

It is pulled from live ads by default.
Each brand can be set to track **Global Ads or EU/UK-only ads**.

Newly added brands can take **hours** before all sections of the overview are filled in.
The brand tracker covers Meta advertisers only.

Each brand page links to the same ads in the Meta Ad Library.
Check the ads directly in the Ad Library before you rely on the tracker data.
Each breakdown tab (a separate section of a brand's overview) offers time filters **7D, 30D, 3M, 6M, Custom and All**. The D means days and the M means months.

Each breakdown tab also has an **Export CSV** button. A CSV is a spreadsheet file.
Sort options include Usage and longest running.

Winning Hunter lets you export a brand's **top hooks, personas and angles**.
Feeding that export into Claude AI (an AI chatbot) can uncover additional personas and angles.

Quick actions for a brand:
Open Brands, select the brand and use the **Quick Actions** menu (a list of shortcuts).
**Track brand** follows the advertiser.

**Track store** does the same for a Shopify store.
**Visit Product Page** opens the store.
**Download Video** and **Download Thumbnail** save creative files.

**Transcribe ad with AI** produces a script of the ad.
Other listed actions include Page Ad Library and Fulfill with Ecommerce.
Winning Hunter (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: The ad details panel shows **running days**. It also shows the number of duplicates (other advertisers using the same creative).
It shows the landing page URL, the product price, estimated monthly traffic (visits per month) and the first and last seen dates.
Use these fields to judge how long and how widely an ad has run.
Winning Hunter's Ad Library filter limits results to **one ad per brand** by default. You see fewer winning ads than exist.

Turn that limit off when you want the full set of matches for a niche search.
The limit is currently active, so expect smaller result counts when scanning.
The Ad Library search in the brand tool has a source dropdown (a menu).
Choose **Meta Ads Library** (marked recommended), Facebook Adspy, Pinterest Ads or TikTok Ads.
Start with Meta Ads Library when you need ads that run on Meta.
The Ad Library filter panel has a **Save current filters** button. A niche search can be reused without setting every field again.

Preset shortcuts (ready-made filter sets) also exist for Week's biggest winners, European winners, US winners, Dropship Ads, Advertorials (long ad articles), Native ads (ads that look like normal content),

Quiz Funnels (ads that send people through quiz questions), Supplements and Top Branded.
Tracked brands can be sorted into folders and boards to keep competitor research organized.

The account in the example allowed up to **200 brands**. It displayed the count as used of limit, such as 2 / 200 brands.
Brands Tracker lets you follow Meta advertisers.
You can organize them into folders and boards. You can also track growth, formats, new ads and added dates per brand.

The screen shows a counter (a number showing how many are used) of **13 / 200 brands**.
This suggests a cap on how many brands one account can follow.
Winning Hunter Brands lets you follow Meta advertisers and organize them into folders and boards. You can also open each brand's details.

The counter shows how many of the **200 brand slots** are in use.
The Transcribe ad with AI action sits in the Quick Actions menu of an ad.
Winning Hunter (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
Longer videos can take about **a minute** to produce the transcript.
Wait until the full script appears before copying it. Then check it against the video.
The ad details panel and Magic AI offer discovery shortcuts.
**Find Competitors with Magic AI** and **Find Shopify Competitors with AI** move you from one winning ad to other advertisers and stores in the same space.

Use them as an alternative way to discover competing brands for a product you already want to research.
Winning Hunter ad cards have three action buttons.

**Save ad** keeps the ad in your library.
**Track in Brand Tracker** opens the advertiser's full ad set.
**Recreate ad with AI** generates a new version of the ad.
Use Save and Track to build a **swipe file** (a saved folder of competitor ads for ideas) before you write your own creatives.

Winning Hunter combines Brand Tracker with Sales Tracker.
Brand Tracker shows a brand's personas, USPs, angles and ad copies.
Sales Tracker shows a store's **revenue estimate**, traffic, apps and pixels (a small tracking code that records visits and sales).
Use it to go from an ad found in the Meta Ads Library to a **full competitor analysis**.

Winning Hunter also includes Trends, similar to Exploding Topics (a tool that spots rising topics).
It also includes an AI ad image generator.
The source presents ad research as **the most used part** of the platform.
Unlimited searches in the TikTok Shop explorer (the product search page for TikTok Shop) are a **Premium-plan** feature.

Heavy product research needs the Premium tier.
The explorer also lists trending products, top sellers and new arrivals. It uses the same filters as the main product table.

Winning Hunter is listed at **$90 per month** on the provider's on-screen list.
It is marked as not included on its sales page.
Check the current list and price on the provider's pricing page before budgeting.
Kalodata and TikTok research: Kalodata
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Kalodata is a TikTok product and ad research tool.

It shows products with their revenue, items sold, average unit price, video and ad counts, and category.
It lets you open the ad videos to study their hooks.
Kalodata shows products with product rank by country, units sold, revenue, average unit price and last-30-day figures. It also shows linked videos and ads.

Use it to check **whether a product sells** before you invest time in building a store.
Kalodata setup:
Set the region to **United States**.

Set the date range to **Last 30 Days**.
Open the Video & Ad tab of the product page.

The example list showed **4,487** video and ad items for one product.
In Kalodata, open the Product Insights panel.
Set the country dropdown to United States to see the product's rank in United States TikTok.
Use the **Last 30 Days, Last 90 days and Last 180 days** filters to compare current and older sales data.

For the example NAD+ berry drink mix, Kalodata showed about **34.92k** items sold.
The average unit price was $23.19. The price range was $26.36 to $78.95.

These figures are for the Last 30 Days window from 07/05/2025 to 08/03/2025.
Its Concentration Rate (L30D), a percentage Kalodata shows for the last 30 days, was **22.3%**.
The NAD+ drops in the other form showed **79%**.
Kalodata limits how many videos you can download **without watermark** (a logo laid over the video). The limit depends on your plan.

When the limit is reached, the tool asks you to buy a recharge plan (extra download credit).
So plan which hook and testimonial clips you need **before downloading**.
Kalodata and TikTok research: Kalodata (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: The Kalodata filter panel has a **Save selected filters** button and a Submit button.
A filter set such as the book research set can be stored and reused instead of rebuilt each time.
The Kalodata product detail page has buttons for Generate Promo Video, View on TikTok, Review Insights and Video Tutorial.

It also has a 'Why is this product underperforming' prompt.
These help with a quick check on a candidate product.

Kalodata has a built-in AI assistant (a chatbot inside the tool). It answers research questions about a selected product or category.
Typical questions include:

Finding the top 10 competitors at the same price.
The main pain points in customer reviews.
Why a product is not selling well and what could change.

A product selection analysis report.
A comparison of the product's competitiveness with a similar product.

The recent **GMV** (gross merchandise value, the total sales value) and sales trends.
The Kalodata product detail page is organized into tabs and panels.
The tabs and panels are: Overview, Product Card, Reviews, Video Content, Video Toolkit, Creator, SKU Analysis (one exact version of a product, such as a size or colour), Concentration, Selling Points

and Review Insights.
The Product Card shows price range, commission rate (the share a promoter earns), shipping fee, rating and creator count.

The Video Toolkit includes Storyboard Export (a plan of the video scenes).
It also includes video generation tools such as Video Remake and Promo Video generation.
Shop information and a Local Shop label also appear on the page.
PP Ads
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
PP Ads offers a product search section and a large TikTok video library for finding ad clips.
It has a trial of **1 USD for 3 days**.
Users sometimes cancel before the trial converts (turns into a paid plan).
PP Ads is a TikTok product and ad research tool. It finds competitor listings and ads for a product.
It typically yields **5 to 50 or more** competitor listings per product. That makes it useful for building a creative folder (a saved folder of ad videos).

PP Ads offers a 3-day trial for **$1**.
After the trial, the subscription bills **$155 per month** unless cancelled.
Cancel the subscription or remove the payment method **before the trial ends**.
Search PP Ads for dropshipper phrasing (the wording dropshippers use in ads, because dropshipping means selling products you do not stock).

Examples: '50% off', 'get yours today' or 'limited time offer'.
This surfaces dropshipping ads.
Branded ads make up most results in broad searches.

So the keyword search finds the right ads **faster**.
PP Ads procedure:
1. Open PP Ads and search **5 to 10** generic keywords from the product's name.
2. Apply the filters: post creation date within the last **two weeks**, around 500 to 1,000 or more likes, and e-commerce platform Shopify.
3. Open the listings with the latest ads. Download the most recent ad videos for a creative folder.
4. Aim for at least **5 to 10** competitor creatives. Use 7 to 10 as a safe range for testing.
Pixta is a product research website and app. It lists products from TikTok ads.
It has tabs such as winning ads and product research.
Each listing links to a TikTok video or ad. This helps you see whether the product is getting traction (gaining attention and sales).
Check the linked content **directly on TikTok**, not only the listing.
TikTok Creative Center, reached through TikTok Business Center (TikTok's business account hub), shows trending hashtags (topic tags that start with #).

It also shows trending songs and top-performing ads.
Use its filters for industry, country and time window to match your **target market**.
Pinterest, multi-platform and other spy tools
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: A spy tool is software that shows what other stores are doing, such as their ads and sales.
Some product research tools have a Pinterest spy feature. It shows which products are running as Pinterest ads right now.
You can filter that Pinterest spy feature by weekly winners, meaning products that did well that week.
Use the Pinterest spy feature to find **test products**, meaning products you try to sell to see if they work.
PPSpy and Ali Hunter estimate a store's sales and its Pinterest activity.
Those Pinterest activity numbers include impressions (how many times an ad was shown) and saves (how many times people saved a pin).

Use these numbers to judge **whether a competitor is performing well**.
Minea is a shop-analysis tool, meaning a tool that studies a store.

Minea fetches a store's ads from most platforms, such as Facebook, TikTok and Pinterest.
Minea shows **how many ads** a store runs and how it grows on Facebook.

This check found **280 ads** for one store.
To analyze a competitor's store in Minea, open **Shops**.
Search for the store name in Shops.

Select the matching result to reach **Shop analysis**.
Shop analysis pulls ads from most platforms and shows how many ads the store runs and how it scales.

For example, one store showed **280 ads**.
Pipiads is most likely the paid product spy tool that shows trending products across platforms.
The source text also writes its name as "pizza".
Pipiads is meant to be added **after you have some experience** with organic content, meaning free posts you publish without paid ads.

Pipiads has a list price of **$263 per month**.
WitTau is a spy tool for YouTube ads.
WitTau shows which product types are working on YouTube.

Pizzazz tracks up to **five competitor stores** at a time.
To track a store in Pizzazz, enter the store's URL, which is its web address.

Pizzazz then shows how many sales the store made in a chosen period.
Pizzazz also has a product spy feature for finding products that are already selling.
Store sales and traffic estimators
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: PPSpy is a free Chrome extension. A Chrome extension is a small add-on for the Google Chrome browser.

PPSpy shows live sales.
PPSpy lets you track **up to five stores for free**.
PPSpy gives sales product by product for the **last 24 hours**.

PPSpy is accurate to roughly **50 to 70 percent**.
PPSpy is listed at **$299 per month** on the bundle list.

The free plan with five tracked stores and the paid list price belong to **different plans**.
Check which plan includes the features you need.
PP Ads estimates how many sales a Shopify store gets. Shopify is an online store platform.

PP Ads records sales **only while the app is open** and you are browsing that store.
Leave PP Ads running for a period, **up to a couple of hours**, before you trust the numbers.
Peak Star estimates the revenue of competitor stores. It does this by scraping their websites. Scraping means copying data from a web page automatically.

A reading of **about 1,000 sales** suggests the store does at least that.
A reading of **1,500 to 2,000 sales** suggests slightly more.

These numbers are rough estimates, not exact figures.
In Peakstar, open the **third menu item**, which is Dashboard, AI content and store research.
Enter the product keyword.

Select the target country, such as **United States**.
This helps you find products you can test.

The seller was unsure whether the store figures show real tracked sales.
So **verify the figures** before you rely on them.
Shop Hunter gives product-level sales for a store. This means sales for each product.
Shop Hunter helps you find the single product that drives the most revenue. Revenue means money coming in.

Use Shop Hunter **together with another tool** to confirm the numbers.
Shop Hunter is an alternative to Peak Star for estimating competitor store sales.
Store sales and traffic estimators (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
Its accuracy compared with other tools was **not verified**.
Peak (peaks) is a product research tool. It shows products being sold and helps you shortlist product ideas.
Peak was combined with **Amazon reviews and Facebook Ads Library checks**. The Facebook Ads Library is a public list of ads that run on Facebook.

To see the **best sellers** of a Shopify store, add a path to the store domain. A domain is the name of a website, such as example.com.
That path is **collections/all**.
Add the setting **sort_by=best-selling** to the end of the address.
Heading note: the following headings are kept as ### for consistency.
Store Tracker is a tool for watching a store over time.
Store Tracker setup has three steps: **Store Tracker > Insert Store URL > Start Tracking**.

After setup, the tracker shows bestsellers, sales, traffic and market data for the store. Traffic means visitors.
Sales Tracker Details shows the store's **launch date**.

It shows the monthly revenue bracket, which is a range of monthly income.
It shows monthly visits.
It shows traffic by country, product and collection counts.

It shows pixels and stack. A pixel is a tracking code that records visits. The stack is the set of tools the store uses.
It shows apps, which are add-ons installed in the store.
It shows similar stores and ad-rank partnership ads, meaning ads run through partner programs.
Use these fields **together** to judge the store's scale and marketing setup.
Website traffic and SimilarWeb
SimilarWeb
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
SimilarWeb is used for competitor research and analysis.
SimilarWeb estimates a store's **monthly traffic**.
SimilarWeb also estimates traffic sources and rough revenue.

Check the **traffic size** before you choose a niche. A niche is a small market focus, such as one product type.
SimilarWeb shows a store's monthly visits.
SimilarWeb splits traffic into direct, search, social and paid sources. Direct means visitors who typed the address. Paid means visitors from paid ads.

SimilarWeb shows the store's country ranking.
Use the country ranking to find the store's **main market** before you choose your own ad country.
SimilarWeb shows a competitor's paid traffic sources and visitor demographics, meaning visitor age, gender and similar details.

SimilarWeb shows the sites where a competitor's ads run.
SimilarWeb shows the **first-seen date** of each ad and how long it has run.

Use it to collect most of the **five campaign variables** in minutes.
At the time of writing, the author prefers SimilarWeb.
If it stops working, **check for alternatives**.

Free search limits differ by route, and the sources give different values:
**SimilarWeb site, free account (2025)**

Free limit: 15 searches per day; no workaround without a paid plan
**SimilarWeb Chrome extension, free tier**

Free limit: 15 searches per week, shown as a counter such as "1 out of 15"
**SimilarWeb free account (2026 advice)**

Free limit: 25 searches per week
Use the limit that matches **the route you are on**.

The 2026 source gives **25 per week** for a free account. It does not name the route.
So **check the limit** shown in your own account.
SimilarWeb Chrome extension
SimilarWeb Chrome extension
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: The SimilarWeb Chrome extension is **free to install** from the Chrome Web Store. The Web Store is Google's shop for browser add-ons.

It shows traffic data for the website open in your browser.
After you click its icon, a panel opens on the right side.
The panel shows global and country traffic ranks. A global rank is a site's popularity worldwide.

The extension means you **do not need** a paid subscription or a free trial account on similarweb.com.
Country check: **scroll down** to the country rank section.
Read the rank for the country where you plan to do business. The example uses the United States.

Install the extension to see a site's traffic and country ranking **without entering a URL**.
Click the icon on the website you are viewing to open a **sidebar**.

Install the SimilarWeb Chrome extension.
Open a competitor's website.
Click the extension icon and **scroll to Country Rank**.

View their ranking in your target country.
If you are not using Chrome, access SimilarWeb.com with a free account.

The extension is free. It needs **no account or email address**.
It works only in Google Chrome.
It returns the same data as the free trial on similarweb.com.

So it is a **fallback** when that trial cannot be set up. A fallback is a backup option.
The extension needs no account or email.

So it avoids the setup problems some users have with the similarweb.com free trial.
Use it as an **alternative route** to the same data when the trial fails.

The extension's ranking section shows a competitor's traffic rank, including the country rank.
It is used to run the **traffic rank test** on future competitors.

The SimilarWeb Chrome extension shows estimated traffic and related website data.
Use it for **competitor and niche research**.
SimilarWeb Chrome extension (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t:
SimilarWeb extension install procedure:
1. Use **Google Chrome** as the browser. If it is missing, download and install it first.
2. Open the **SimilarWeb Website Traffic and SEO Checker** listing in the Chrome Web Store. If no link is at hand, search Google for "SimilarWeb Chrome extension".

SEO means search engine optimization, which is getting found on Google.
3. Click **"Add to Chrome"**.
4. Click **"Add extension"** in the confirmation prompt.

5. Click the **Extensions icon** in the Chrome toolbar and find SimilarWeb in the list.
6. Click **"Pin"** so the extension stays in the navigation bar. Its icon is a blue and orange logo.
Alexa
Alexa.com's free version shows the **global rank** of a competitor's website.

A global rank **inside one million** is considered enough traffic to be worth studying.
The tool does not show exact visitor numbers.
This is older advice from 2018.
Use a competitor research tool that **combines domain rank data** instead of paying for Alexa.

If a supplier or competitor domain shows **no global or domestic rank** there, it is simply not ranked.
This is older advice from 2019.

Checking a competitor's traffic rank on Alexa.com:
1. Open **Alexa.com** and scroll to the bottom right of the page.
2. Click **Browse or Search Sites**.

3. Type the competitor's domain name and click **Find**.
4. Read the **global rank**. If it is inside one million, the site gets enough traffic to be worth your attention.

A competitor research tool returns **no data** when a competitor site is too small.
Try **larger websites** in the niche instead.

A missing result means there is not enough volume for that site. Volume means how much traffic there is.
This is older advice from 2021.
Technology stack lookups
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: BuiltWith (builtwith.com) is a free tool.

BuiltWith identifies all software, platforms and tools used by any website. A platform is the system a store is built on.
Search a competitor's domain in BuiltWith.
BuiltWith shows their **Shopify version**, apps, payment processors and other integrations. An integration is a tool linked to the store.

BuiltWith is a website lookup tool.
It shows which platforms, apps and technologies a competitor's site uses.
BuiltWith is a free website.

It shows the apps and technologies used on any URL.
For example, it shows the **Shopify apps** on a competitor's store.
Cold-email agencies use the same kind of tool to contact every Shopify store. This is why such outreach happens.

BuiltWith can show which apps and technologies a Shopify or other website uses.
This helps identify stores **built recently by agencies**.
Cola is a Chrome extension.
Cola shows which apps a store has installed.
Use Cola on a competitor's store to see **whether it runs a print-on-demand supplier app**. Print-on-demand means items are printed only after an order comes in.
Some apps stay **undetected**.

Pricing and testing apps seen on competitor stores include Intelligems. Intelligems is used for **A/B testing** of pricing and layouts. A/B testing means showing two versions to split visitors and compare results.
Kaching Bundles is used for **quantity-break bundles**. These are discounts for buying more.
Marketing and review apps seen on competitor stores include Klaviyo. Klaviyo sends **email and SMS**, which are text messages.

Judge.me is used for **product reviews**.
A Product Amazon Reviews app is used for **importing reviews**.
Triple Whale is used for **analytics**, which means measuring store numbers.
Competitor creative research, swipe files and monitoring
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: A swipe board saves competitor ads into boards for later reference. A swipe file is a collection of saved examples.

The Foreplay app is one example of a swipe board.
Build **one board per angle or per competitor**. An angle is the reason or hook used in an ad.

This way, creative briefs start from **real examples**. A creative brief is a short plan for an ad.
Clipping services collect everything published about a product category.

This includes competitor ads and claims.
Use clipping services as a source of **competitive research before writing ads**.

Google Chrome's "Search image with Google" finds the same product image on other sites.
To use it, **right-click an image**.

This often reveals the **brand name** of a product.
AMZ Shark and AMZ Tracker track competitor products.

They show sales velocity, which means how fast a product sells. They also show reviews, pricing and trends over time.
They are useful for **ongoing competitive monitoring**.

They are **not essential** when starting.
SearchMonitor is a paid tool.
It monitors competitors' Product Listing Ads. These are paid product ads in search results.
It can flag sellers pricing **below MAP**. MAP means minimum advertised price, the lowest price a seller may show.
It replaces manual SKU-by-SKU price checks. A SKU is a product code, so this means checking each product code by hand.

It is an option for stores that want **constant price data**.
The alternative is to audit ad accounts **every one to two weeks**. To audit means to review.

Investigate when **sales drop**.
This can reveal a competitor breaking MAP by **around 10%**.
This is older advice from 2022.

Amazon publishes a fee lookup tool on its seller site.
Use it to check **all fees** for a product.

Do this **before choosing a niche and calculating profit**.
The Amazon Best Sellers page shows the **top 100 products** in each category.
It also shows the subcategories.

Use it to find product ideas and check what sells.
Seller Pulse is an Amazon research tool.
Seller Pulse is used to find **top-selling products** on the marketplace.
Amazon research tools (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Amazon Ads sponsored listings are **paid placements** that put products at the top of search results.
Jungle Scout is a product research tool for FBA. FBA means Fulfilled by Amazon, where Amazon stores and ships orders.

Like AMZ Shark, Jungle Scout is helpful for detailed analysis.
It is **not required** to launch your first product.
Review Index is a Chrome extension.

It adds a summarize button to an Amazon listing.
It shows the **pros and cons** from customer reviews.
This helps spot **common complaints**.

Amazon Reviews Summarizer setup: **install the Chrome extension**.
To find it, search "amazon review summarizer" on Google and open the **first result**.

On an Amazon product page, click the extension's summary **just below the product name and price**.
It lists the pros and cons customers mention.
A ChatGPT plugin reads Amazon reviews. A plugin is an add-on for ChatGPT.

That plugin returned summary themes such as product quality, effectiveness and a self-cleaning feature.
These themes were judged **shallow**.

Export all reviews to a spreadsheet with a Chrome extension.
Paste them into ChatGPT **in batches**, meaning small groups.

This gave **richer audience insight**.
Axiom is a browser extension.
It scrapes product review data into **Google Sheets**. Google Sheets is a free online spreadsheet.

You choose fields such as star rating, date and review text on a product page.
Procedure for scraping product reviews with the Axiom extension:
1. Open the Axiom extension on the product page and click **Get current URL**.
2. Click **Select** for the first review field, such as star rating. Then click a second matching element so the rest **auto-fills**.

3. Repeat for other fields such as date and review text. Click **two matching elements** each time.
4. Set the **scrape limit**, such as 20 reviews.
5. If reviews are paginated, meaning split over several pages, click **Find pager**. Then select the show more reviews button so the extension moves through all pages.
6. Click **Complete**. Then paste the results into Google Sheets and sort by the rating column.

Tool bundles and their costs (continued)
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: The claimed saving of **$2,000 to $3,000 per month** only holds for a buyer who would otherwise pay for most of these tools.
The claimed monthly savings of $2,000 to $3,000 assume the buyer would otherwise pay for **almost all** listed tools.

A seller who uses only **two or three** of them saves far less than the headline figure.
The savings claimed for a bundle are measured against **buying every tool at list price**.
The real saving for one seller is the list price of the tools they would have bought anyway, **minus what they pay**.
Shared subscriptions only save money on tools you would actually use.
Extras advertised with a bundle are marketing claims. Examples are 10,000+ templates, 10,000+ paid courses, 1,600+ Shopify themes or a winning product every day.

These extras have **no cash value** in a savings calculation unless you use them.
**Do not add** them to the savings total.

Before paying for a bundle, check the **promo codes** at checkout. A promo code is a discount code.
The codes differ. One is ecommerce10. The sales page shows Source D10.
Confirm which code is accepted and **what discount it gives** on the final price before you rely on it.

The bundle promises **24/7 access with no downtime**. Downtime means the service is not working.
It promises multiple accounts when needed.
It promises shared credentials with auto login. Credentials are login details. Auto login logs you in for you.

It promises new tools every month and quick support for anything.
No uptime percentage is stated. Uptime is how often the service works.

No support response time is stated.
No notice period for removed tools is stated.
Treat these as promises that need **written confirmation before you pay**.
Shared accounts and their risks
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Shared-account services such as ShareTool split the cost of an ad account among several users.

An ad account is the account used to run paid ads.
For example, a tool priced at about 100 per month can cost about **20 per month** when five users share it.

Shared accounts are much cheaper.
But **other users can see anything saved** in them.
Do **not save winning products** inside a shared ad account.
Keep saved product research in your own browser or elsewhere.
Access through shared accounts is **not guaranteed**. This is true even when a bundle promises 24/7 access and no downtime.
A suspended shared account can cut off a whole workflow. A workflow is a set of steps you repeat.

So **export and save** research data locally, meaning on your own computer.
Avoid building a single critical process on **one shared login**.
The tool list here serves four main jobs.
The four jobs are product and ad spying, keyword and SEO research, Amazon product research, and content creation.
Product and ad spying tools: Pipiads, PPSpy, Adspy, Dropispy, Foreplay, Adsparo, Pinspy, Peeksta, Dropship.io, Shophunter, Kalodata, NicheScraper.
Keyword and SEO research tools: Answer The Public, WooRank, SpyFu, Exploding Topics. Keywords are the words people type into search.
Amazon product research tool: Helium 10.
Design, video, audio and AI content creation tools: Canva Pro, Capcut Pro, Clipchamp, Picsart, Photoroom, Runway, Submagic, ElevenLabs, Midjourney, Pika Art.

Rules for subscriptions:
1. **Match each subscription** to the job it does for your store.
2. **Cancel any tool** that has no current job.
PeakStar's TikTok ads search finds running dropshipping ads.
p.h: TikTok shop and ad discovery tools

p.t:
Dropshipping means selling products you do not stock yourself.
You can filter these ads by country, like count, recency and keywords.

PPAds is a larger ad library used for the same purpose.
PPAds has offered a trial with **full access for 3 days**.
The trial price was **$1** earlier and later **$7**.

The figure that applies **depends on when you sign up**.
FastMoss is used for product research.
It scans TikTok Shop and Shopify data.
It reveals **trending products** and their sales figures instantly.
Kalodata
p.s: Product, competitor and ad research tools

p.t: Kalodata is a research tool (a website that collects data for you) for TikTok Shop (TikTok's built-in online store).
It **ranks** products, videos and creators by revenue (money earned from sales), views and ad metrics (numbers that show how well ads perform).
**Set the region to United States** before you read any ranking. A region is the country or market the data comes from, and results differ by market.
**Newer versions** add a product detail summary (a short overview of one product) and a buyer review summary (a short overview of customer reviews).

**Filter groups** are sets of settings that narrow the results. These are the filter groups in the 2025 version of Kalodata:
Short meanings for the terms in the table:

**ROAS** (return on ad spend): money earned for each unit of money spent on ads.
**Organic traffic**: visitors who arrive without paid ads.

**Affiliate**: a person paid a share of sales for promoting a product.
**Creator**: a person who posts videos to promote products.

**Conversion ratio**: the share of viewers who go on to buy.
**Uptrend**: a number that is going up over time.
**Livestream**: a live video where products are sold in real time.
**Dropshipping**: you sell a product, and a supplier ships it to the customer. You do not keep stock yourself.

**Local warehouse dropshipping**: dropshipping where the products are stored in a warehouse close to the customer.
**Dates**: Last 30 Days
**Revenue Filters**: Revenue Uptrend, Revenue Growth, Revenue

**Video filters**: High ROAS, High Organic Traffic Sales Videos, Low-Follower Sales Videos, Video & Ad Livestream
**Ad Filters**: Ad Spend, Ad ROAS, Ad View Ratio
**Creator filters**: Creator Debut Time, Creator Followers, Creator Number, Creator Conversion Ratio

**Category and shop**: Category (search by category name), Shop Creator
**Pricing**: Pricing (price range)
**Product tabs**: Top New Products, High Potential Affiliate, Sales Grow Rapidly, Top Video Products, Local Warehouse Dropshipping
**Advanced**: Advanced, Save selected filters
A niche is a small, specific product market. AI-assisted means you use an AI tool to help you do the work.
**ChatGPT** (an AI chat tool) can write a rough market analysis (a study of who buys and who sells) of a niche. It can also name the top competitors (the biggest rival sellers) and top brands.
The output is **not fully reliable**. Use it only as a starting point, then check it against real analytics (real sales and traffic numbers from tools or your own store).
